name: ENT & audiology (category guide)
summary: Private ENT vs polyclinic referral — tinnitus / sinus / hearing-aid fitting honesty, audiologist vs ENT roles, and insurer specialist rules.
body: Ear, nose and throat complaints (sinus, sleep apnoea screens, tinnitus, sudden hearing loss) are a frequent expat specialist hop. Public path is GP/polyclinic → hospital ENT; foreigners pay full fees and wait. Private ENT buys speed and MRI coordination; verify SMC Otolaryngology registration before you book. Audiologists handle hearing tests and hearing-aid fitting — that is allied-health territory, not a substitute for urgent ENT when hearing drops suddenly (same-day / A&E rules apply). Hearing-aid retail hard-sells are a forum theme: ask for unaided audiogram copies, trial periods, and written aftercare fees. Group plans often need a GP referral before specialist reimbursement and may exclude hearing aids entirely — read the schedule. This guide is not IVF, derm, or screening packages; keep those in their own directory entries. Category guide, not a ranked ENT list.
